title: Dialogue & characters

body.text: Characters come alive when they have a
character sheet: goal, wound, fear, and a distinctive way of speaking
— build it with the AI and use it as a reference throughout the story, so the dialogue never breaks character.

example: "Create a character sheet for the protagonist: a 50-year-old rural doctor who lost his son, speaks little, falls back on 'we'll see how it goes' when dodging anything sad"

title: Test dialogue by role-playing

body.text: have the AI play the character and talk to it
— ask hard questions and see if the answers fit; it helps you find the character's true voice before writing for real.

example: "Play this doctor — I'm a reporter asking about his son — answer the way this character really would"

question: What should a character sheet include?

options.text: Goal, emotional wound, fear, and a distinctive way of speaking

question: How do you test a character's voice?

options.text: Have the AI play the character and talk to it

question: What does a character sheet help with in a long story?

options.text: Dialogue stays consistent and in character

question: To test a character's dialogue for realism, what should you do?

options.text: Have Claude play the character and try a conversation

question: What does good dialogue and character design help with?

options.text: Characters get a distinctive, believable voice
